Captain George Vancouver claims Puget Sound for the Kingdom of Great Britain.

Massachusetts becomes the first state of the United States to set a minimum wage.

Women's suffrage in the United States

links.t: Regional Congress of Peasants, Workers and Insurgents

main.t: President of the Republic of China

links.t: We shall fight on the beaches

links.t: House of Commons of the United Kingdom

main.desc: 1942 major naval battle in World War II

A military coup in Argentina ousts Ramón Castillo.

main.desc: 1943 military coup against Argentine President Ramón Castillo

events.text: World War II: A United States Navy task group captured German submarine U-505 (pictured).

main.desc: Theater Army of the U.S. Army

events.text: in Argentina assumes its first presidency Juan Domingo Perón.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: A chartered British Midland Airways aircraft crashed near Stockport, England, killing 72 of the 84 people on board.

Tonga gains independence from the British Empire.
Major League Baseball's Cleveland Indians hosted Ten-Cent Beer Night, but had to forfeit the game to the Texas Rangers due to rioting by drunken fans.

JVC introduces its VHS videotape at the Consumer Electronics Show in Chicago. It will eventually prevail against Sony's rival Betamax system in a format war to become the predominant home video medium.
Jerry Rawlings came to power in Ghana as chairman of the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council.

main.desc: Leader of Ghana in 1979 and from 1981 to 2001

Gordon Kahl, who killed two US Marshals in Medina, North Dakota on February 13, is killed in a shootout in Smithville, Arkansas, along with a local sheriff, after a four-month manhunt.
Jonathan Pollard pleads guilty to espionage for selling top secret United States military intelligence to Israel.

links.t: People's Liberation Army at the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre

main.desc: 1989 railway accident in Iglinksy District, Bashkir SSR, Soviet Union

Terry Nichols was sentenced to life in prison for his role in the Oklahoma City bombing.
In Granby, Colorado, U.S., Marvin Heemeyer went on a rampage with a modified bulldozer over a zoning dispute, destroying several buildings before dying by suicide.

Tutush, brother of Seljuk sultan Malik Shah, defeats Suleiman ibn Qutalmish, the Turkish ruler of Anatolia in the battle of Ain Salm.
Bolesław V, High Duke of Poland, granted city rights to Kraków modelled on the Magdeburg town charter.

Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery serial, Uncle Tom's Cabin, or Life Among the Lowly, starts a ten-month run in the National Era abolitionist newspaper.

Sultan Barghash bin Said of Zanzibar closes the great slave market under the terms of a treaty with Great Britain.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1961 to 1963

events.text: World War II veteran Walter Seifert attacks an elementary school in Cologne, Germany, killing at least eight children and two teachers, and seriously injuring several more, with a home-made flamethrower and a lance.

main.desc: 1964 mass murder at an elementary school in Cologne, West Germany

events.text: Lloyd J. Old identifies the first cell surface antigens that could differentiate among different cell types.
After being appointed on May 15, Anna Mae Hays and Elizabeth P. Hoisington officially receive their ranks as U.S. Army general officers, becoming the first women to do so.
The U.S. Government forcibly removes the last holdouts to the Native American Occupation of Alcatraz, ending 19 months of control.
Altaf Hussain founds the student political movement All Pakistan Muhajir Students Organisation (APMSO) in Karachi University.

main.desc: British Pakistani politician; founder of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (born 1953)

events.text: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake at Golbaf, Iran, kills at least 2,000.
Diane Abbott, Paul Boateng and Bernie Grant are elected as the first black MPs in Great Britain.
Compaq Computer pays US$9 billion for Digital Equipment Corporation in the largest high-tech acquisition.
Timothy McVeigh, detonator of a truck bomb in front of the Oklahoma federal building, was executed by lethal injection for using a weapon of mass destruction, among other charges.
Robert Edward Dyer was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for conducting a six-month-long letter-bomb campaign against the British supermarket chain Tesco.
Timothy McVeigh is executed for his role in the Oklahoma City bombing.
Antonio Meucci is acknowledged as the first inventor of the telephone by the United States Congress.
Cassini–Huygens makes its closest flyby of the Saturn moon Phoebe.
Mudslides caused by heavy monsoon rainfall and exacerbated by hill cutting killed at least 128 people in Chittagong, Bangladesh.
Mudslides in Chittagong, Bangladesh, kill 130 people.
Canadian prime minister Stephen Harper apologised to the First Nations for past governments' policies of forced assimilation.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Canada from 2006 to 2015

events.text: Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper makes a historic official apology to Canada's First Nations in regard to abuses at a Canadian Indian residential school.
The Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope is launched into orbit.

main.desc: Space telescope for gamma-ray astronomy launched in 2008

events.text: The first FIFA World Cup held on African soil kicks off in South Africa.
Two earthquakes struck northern Afghanistan, triggering a massive landslide that buried a village and killed 75 people.
Seventy-five people die in a landslide triggered by two earthquakes in Afghanistan; an entire village is buried.
Greece's public broadcaster ERT is shut down by then-prime minister Antonis Samaras. It would be opened exactly two years later by then-prime minister Alexis Tsipras.
Battle of Augsburg: The Hungarians defeat the East Frankish army under King Louis the Child, using the famous feigned retreat tactic of the nomadic warriors.

main.desc: Battle during the Hungarian invasions of Europe

events.text: Constantine IX Monomachos is crowned as Byzantine Emperor, one day after his marriage to Empress Zoe Porphyrogenita.
The Ghurid general Qutb ud-Din Aibak founds the Delhi Sultanate.

main.desc: Late 8th-century–1215 Iranian dynasty from Ghor, modern Afghanistan

events.text: The Disputation of Paris, in which four rabbis defended the Talmud against Nicholas Donin's accusations of blasphemy, began in the court of King Louis IX.

main.desc: Disputation over the Talmud at the court of French King Louis IX (1240)

events.text: At the instigation of Louis IX of France, an inter-faith debate, known as the Disputation of Paris, starts between a Christian monk and four rabbis.
Peasants' Revolt: In England, rebels assemble at Blackheath, just outside London.
Armagnac–Burgundian Civil War: Parisians slaughter sympathizers of Bernard VII, Count of Armagnac, along with all prisoners, foreign bankers, and students and faculty of the College of Navarre.
Hundred Years' War: On the second day of the Battle of Jargeau, Joan of Arc leads the French army in their capture of the city and the English commander, William de la Pole, 1st Duke of Suffolk.

links.t: William de la Pole, 1st Duke of Suffolk

events.text: The city of Helsinki, Finland (belonging to Sweden at the time) is founded by King Gustav I of Sweden.

main.desc: Capital and most populous city of Finland

events.text: The Westminster Assembly is convened by the Parliament of England, without the assent of Charles I, in order to restructure the Church of England.
First Anglo-Dutch War: The Battle of the Gabbard begins, lasting until the following day.

main.desc: Conflict between the Commonwealth and the Dutch Republic

events.text: Thomas Willett is appointed the first mayor of New York City.

main.desc: 1st and 3rd Mayor of New York City (1665–66, 1667–68)

events.text: French and Indian War: Siege of Louisbourg: James Wolfe's attack at Louisbourg, Nova Scotia, commences.

main.desc: North American theater of the Seven Years' War

events.text: French explorer Marc-Joseph Marion du Fresne and 25 of his men are killed by Māori in New Zealand.
Thomas Gage, the governor of the Province of Massachusetts Bay, offered a general pardon to colonists who remained loyal to Britain.

main.desc: British Army officer and colonial administrator (1718/19–1787)

events.text: American War of Independence: British general Thomas Gage declares martial law in Massachusetts. The British offer a pardon to all colonists who lay down their arms. There would be only two exceptions to the amnesty: Samuel Adams and John Hancock, if captured, were to be hanged.
The Fifth Virginia Convention adopted a declaration of rights, an influential document that proclaimed the inherent rights of men.

main.desc: Meeting of the Patriot legislature of Virginia in 1776

events.text: The Virginia Declaration of Rights is adopted.
Following the successful French invasion of Malta, the Knights Hospitaller surrendered Malta to Napoleon, initiating two years of occupation.

main.desc: 1798 invasion, part of the Mediterranean campaign

events.text: Irish Rebellion of 1798: Battle of Ballynahinch.

main.desc: Part of the French Revolutionary Wars

events.text: War of 1812: Capture of USRC Surveyor.
The earliest form of bicycle, the dandy horse, is driven by Karl von Drais.
Badi VII, king of Sennar, surrenders his throne and realm to Isma'il Pasha, general of the Ottoman Empire, ending the existence of that Sudanese kingdom.

main.desc: Final ruler of the Funj Sultanate from 1805 to 1821

events.text: Beginning of the Invasion of Algiers: Thirty-four thousand French soldiers land 27 kilometers west of Algiers, at Sidi Ferruch.

main.desc: 1830 campaign of the French conquest of Algeria

events.text: Union general Ulysses S. Grant pulled his troops out of the Battle of Cold Harbor in Hanover County, Virginia, ending one of the bloodiest, most lopsided battles in the American Civil War.

American Civil War, Overland Campaign: Battle of Cold Harbor: Ulysses S. Grant gives the Confederate forces under Robert E. Lee a victory when he pulls his Union troops from their position at Cold Harbor, Virginia and moves south.
Philippine Declaration of Independence: General Emilio Aguinaldo declares the Philippines' independence from Spain.

main.desc: 1898 assertion of Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule

events.text: New Richmond tornado: The ninth deadliest tornado in U.S. history kills 117 people and injures around 200.

main.desc: Severe windstorm in Wisconsin, United States

events.text: The Reichstag approves new legislation continuing Germany's naval expansion program, providing for construction of 38 battleships over a 20-year period. Germany's fleet would be the largest in the world.

main.desc: Seat of the federal parliament of Germany

events.text: As part of the Ottoman Empire's policies of ethnic cleansing, Turkish irregulars began a six-day massacre in the predominantly Greek town of Phocaea.
Massacre of Phocaea: Turkish irregulars slaughter 50 to 100 Greeks and expel thousands of others in an ethnic cleansing operation in the Ottoman Empire.

main.desc: 1914 killing of Greeks in the Ottoman Empire

events.text: Soviet politician Vladimir Antonov-Ovseenko authorised the use of chemical weapons against a peasant rebellion in the Tambov Governorate.
Mikhail Tukhachevsky orders the use of chemical weapons against the Tambov Rebellion, bringing an end to the peasant uprising.
A ceasefire is negotiated between Bolivia and Paraguay, ending the Chaco War.
Shooting begins on Paramount Pictures' Dr. Cyclops, the first horror film photographed in three-strip Technicolor.
The Baseball Hall of Fame opens in Cooperstown, New York.

main.t: National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum
main.desc: Professional sports hall of fame in New York, U.S.

events.text: World War II: Thirteen thousand British and French troops surrender to General Erwin Rommel at Saint-Valery-en-Caux.
On her thirteenth birthday, Anne Frank (pictured) began keeping a diary during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands in World War II.

links.t: The Diary of a Young Girl

events.text: Anne Frank receives a diary for her thirteenth birthday.
The Holocaust: Germany liquidates the Jewish Ghetto in Brzeżany, Poland (now Berezhany, Ukraine). Around 1,180 Jews are led to the city's old Jewish graveyard and shot.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: World War II: Battle of Carentan: American paratroopers of the 101st Airborne Division secure the town of Carentan, Normandy, France.
An Air France Douglas DC-4 crashes near Bahrain International Airport, killing 46 people.

main.t: 1950 Bahrain Air France Douglas DC-4 crashes
main.desc: Pair of aircraft accidents in Bahrain

events.text: Dominic Savio, who was 14 years old at his death in 1857, was canonized by Pope Pius XII, making him one of the youngest non-martyred saints in the Catholic Church.

Pope Pius XII canonises Dominic Savio, who was 14 years old at the time of his death, as a saint, making him at the time the youngest unmartyred saint in the Roman Catholic Church. In 2017, Francisco and Jacinta Marto, aged ten and nine at the time of their deaths, are declared as saints.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1939 to 1958

events.text: The premiere was held in New York of the historical drama film Cleopatra, the most expensive film made to that point.
NAACP field secretary Medgar Evers is murdered in front of his home in Jackson, Mississippi, by Ku Klux Klan member Byron De La Beckwith during the civil rights movement.
The film Cleopatra, starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, is released in US theaters. It was the most expensive film made at the time.

Anti-apartheid activist and ANC leader Nelson Mandela's original 5-year sentence is extended to life sentence for high treason together with Denis Goldberg, Ahmed Kathrada, Govan Mbeki, Raymond Mhlaba, Andrew Mlangeni, Elias Motsoaledi and Walter Sisulu in the Rivonia Trial for sabotage in South Africa.

main.desc: South African system of racial segregation

events.text: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down laws restricting interracial marriage in the landmark civil rights case Loving v. Virginia.

main.t: Supreme Court of the United States
main.desc: Highest court of jurisdiction in the U.S.

links.t: Anti-miscegenation laws in the United States

events.text: The United States Supreme Court in Loving v. Virginia declares all U.S. state laws that prohibit interracial marriage to be unconstitutional.

main.t: Supreme Court of the United States
main.desc: Highest court of jurisdiction in the U.S.

events.text: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain: Judge Jagmohanlal Sinha rules against Indira Gandhi in a case on her election to the Indian Parliament, and that she should be banned from holding any public office, triggering a political crisis.

main.t: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain

events.text: American serial killer David Berkowitz, popularly known as the "Son of Sam", was sentenced to 25-years-to-life in prison for each of six killings.
Bryan Allen wins the second Kremer prize for a man-powered flight across the English Channel in the Gossamer Albatross.
Raiders of the Lost Ark, the first film in the Indiana Jones franchise, was released.
The first of the Indiana Jones film franchise, Raiders of the Lost Ark, is released in theaters.
A nuclear disarmament rally and concert is held in New York City.

main.desc: Most populous city in the United States

events.text: Cold War: During a speech at the Brandenburg Gate by the Berlin Wall, US president Ronald Reagan challenged Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev to "tear down this wall!" (speech featured).

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: The Central African Republic's former emperor Jean-Bédel Bokassa is sentenced to death for crimes he had committed during his 13-year rule.
Cold War: At the Brandenburg Gate, U.S. President Ronald Reagan publicly challenges Mikhail Gorbachev to tear down the Berlin Wall.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 046, a McDonnell Douglas MD-81, crashes short of the runway at Libertador General José de San Martín Airport, killing all 22 people on board.

links.t: Libertador General José de San Martín Airport

events.text: Russia Day: The parliament of the Russian Federation formally declares its sovereignty.

main.desc: National holiday of the Russian Federation (12 June)

events.text: More than 150 Sri Lankan Tamil civilians were massacred by members of the military in the village of Kokkadichcholai.
In modern Russia's first democratic election, Boris Yeltsin is elected as the President of Russia.
Kokkadichcholai massacre: The Sri Lankan Army massacres 152 minority Tamil civilians in the village of Kokkadichcholai near the Eastern Province town of Batticaloa.

main.desc: 1991 mass killing of Sri Lankan Tamils by the Sri Lankan military

events.text: An election takes place in Nigeria and is won by Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola. Its results are later annulled by the military government of Ibrahim Babangida.
The Boeing 777, the world's largest twinjet, made its maiden flight.
In the aftermath of the bombing of Yugoslavia and the Kosovo War, the NATO-led Kosovo Force entered the territory with a mandate of establishing a secure environment.
Kosovo War: Operation Joint Guardian begins when a NATO-led United Nations peacekeeping force, Kosovo Force (KFor), enters the province of Kosovo in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
A disputed presidential election in Iran leads to wide-ranging local and international protests.
Sixteen-year-old Abby Sunderland was rescued after her boat was dismasted in the Indian Ocean while trying to become the youngest sailor around the world.

Between 1,095 and 1,700 Shia Iraqi people are killed in an attack by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant on Camp Speicher in Tikrit, Iraq. It is the second deadliest act of terrorism in history, only behind 9/11.
An Islamic terrorist killed 49 people in a mass shooting at the gay nightclub Pulse in Orlando, Florida.
Forty-nine civilians are killed and 58 others injured in an attack on a gay nightclub in Orlando, Florida, United States; the gunman, Omar Mateen, is killed in a gunfight with police.
United States President Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un of North Korea hold the first meeting between leaders of their two countries in Singapore.
Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is inaugurated as the second president of Kazakhstan.
A fire in a residential building in Mangaf, Kuwait City kills at least 50 people.
Air India Flight 171 (wreckage pictured) crashed shortly after take-off in Ahmedabad, India, killing 260 people.

Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, crashes shortly after takeoff into the B. J. Medical College, Ahmedabad, India, killing 241 out of 242 onboard as well as 19 on the ground. This marked the first fatal crash and hull loss of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner.
South African-American businessman Elon Musk becomes the first US$ trillionaire with the initial public offering of SpaceX.
The decisions of the Edict of Milan, signed by Constantine the Great and co-emperor Valerius Licinius, granting religious freedom throughout the Roman Empire, are published in Nicomedia.

main.desc: Legalization of Christianity in the Roman Empire (313)

events.text: Ibn Battuta begins his travels, leaving his home in Tangiers to travel to Mecca (gone 24 years).
In England, the Peasants' Revolt, led by Wat Tyler, comes to a head, as rebels set fire to the Savoy Palace.
Henry Grace à Dieu, the largest warship ever built at the time, was launched from Woolwich Dockyard, England.
Henry Grace à Dieu, at over 1,000 tons the largest warship in the world at this time, built at the new Woolwich Dockyard in England, is dedicated.
Martin Luther married Katharina von Bora, beginning the practice of clerical marriage in Protestantism.
Martin Luther marries Katharina von Bora, against the celibacy rule decreed by the Roman Catholic Church for priests and nuns.
King Charles I of England marries Catholic princess Henrietta Maria of France and Navarre, at Canterbury.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1625 to 1649

events.text: Georgia provincial governor James Oglethorpe begins an unsuccessful attempt to take Spanish Florida during the Siege of St. Augustine.
Rhode Island becomes the first of Britain's North American colonies to ban the importation of slaves.
American Revolutionary War: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette lands near Charleston, South Carolina, in order to help the Continental Congress to train its army.
Lewis and Clark Expedition: Meriwether Lewis became the first white American to sight the Great Falls of the Missouri River.
Lewis and Clark Expedition: Scouting ahead of the expedition, Meriwether Lewis and four companions sight the Great Falls of the Missouri River.
The American League of Colored Laborers, one of the first labor unions for African Americans, was established in New York City.

main.desc: Former labor union of the United States

events.text: The American League of Colored Laborers, the first African American labor union in the United States, is established in New York City.

main.desc: Former labor union of the United States

events.text: Twentieth opera of Giuseppe Verdi, Les vêpres siciliennes ("The Sicilian Vespers"), is premiered in Paris.
Start of the Congress of Berlin in which the major powers of Europe revise the Treaty of San Stefano, signed on March 3 the same year, that Russia had imposed on a defeated Ottoman Empire.

main.desc: 1878 meeting of representatives of the major European powers

events.text: The Jeannette expedition to reach the North Pole from the Pacific Ocean via the Bering Strait came to an end when the USS Jeannette (pictured), after having been trapped in ice for almost two years, was crushed and sank.
The USS Jeannette is crushed in an Arctic Ocean ice pack.
A fire devastates much of Vancouver, British Columbia.

main.desc: 1886 fire that burned down most of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

events.text: Grover Cleveland notices a rough spot in his mouth and on July 1 undergoes secret, successful surgery to remove a large, cancerous portion of his jaw; the operation was not revealed to the public until 1917, nine years after the president's death.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1885 to 1889 and from 1893 to 1897

events.text: Émile Levassor wins the world's first real automobile race. Levassor completed the 732-mile course, from Paris to Bordeaux and back, in just under 49 hours, at a then-impressive speed of about fifteen miles per hour (24 km/h).
Yukon Territory is formed, with Dawson chosen as its capital.
The Workers' Federation of Chile declares a general strike in solidarity with an ongoing rail workers' strike.
The Workers' Federation of Chile declares a general strike in solidarity with a rail workers' strike.
World War I: The Battle of Mont Sorrel in the Ypres Salient came to an end as a Canadian assault led German forces to withdraw to their original lines.
World War I: The deadliest German air raid on London of the war is carried out by Gotha G.IV bombers and results in 162 deaths, including 46 children, and 432 injuries.
Aviator Charles Lindbergh receives a ticker tape parade up 5th Avenue in New York City.
In one of the biggest upsets in championship boxing, the underdog James J. Braddock defeated Max Baer to become the heavyweight champion of the world.

links.t: List of world heavyweight boxing champions

events.text: Second World War: At the Battle of Villers-Bocage, German tank commander Michael Wittmann destroyed around 30 Allied vehicles in less than 15 minutes.

World War II: The Battle of Villers-Bocage:  German tank ace Michael Wittmann ambushes elements of the British 7th Armoured Division, destroying up to fourteen tanks, fifteen personnel carriers and two anti-tank guns in a Tiger I tank.
World War II: German combat elements, reinforced by the 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division, launch a counterattack on American forces near Carentan.

main.t: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen

events.text: World War II: Germany launches the first V1 Flying Bomb attack on England. Only four of the eleven bombs strike their targets.

main.desc: German World War II cruise missile

events.text: Soviet aircraft shot down a Swedish military plane carrying out signals-intelligence gathering operations, followed three days later by the shootdown of a second plane searching for the first one.
Catalina affair: A Swedish Douglas DC-3 is shot down by a Soviet MiG-15 fighter.
Spanish football club Real Madrid CF wins the inaugural European Cup, UEFA's premier club competition, by winning 4–3 against French club Stade de Reims in the final.
The United States Supreme Court rules in Miranda v. Arizona that the police must inform suspects of their Fifth Amendment rights before questioning them (colloquially known as "Mirandizing").

main.t: Supreme Court of the United States
main.desc: Highest court of jurisdiction in the U.S.

links.t: Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution

events.text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson nominates Solicitor-General Thurgood Marshall to become the first black justice on the U.S. Supreme Court.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1963 to 1969

links.t: Supreme Court of the United States

events.text: Preston Smith, Governor of Texas, signed a law converting a research arm of Texas Instruments into the University of Texas at Dallas.
"The Long and Winding Road" became the Beatles' twentieth and final number-one single on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

The New York Times published the first excerpts from the Pentagon Papers, a 7,000-page classified Department of Defense history of the United States' political and military involvement in the Vietnam War.
Vietnam War: The New York Times begins publication of the Pentagon Papers.

In a game versus the Philadelphia Phillies at Veterans Stadium, Los Angeles Dodgers teammates Steve Garvey, Davey Lopes, Ron Cey and Bill Russell play together as an infield for the first time, going on to set the Major League Baseball record of staying together for 8+1⁄2 years.

links.t: Dodger infield of Garvey, Lopes, Cey and Russell

events.text: Convicted Martin Luther King Jr. assassin James Earl Ray is recaptured after escaping from prison three days before.

main.desc: American minister and civil rights activist (1929–1968)

events.text: English teenager Marcus Sarjeant fired six blanks at Queen Elizabeth II as she rode down The Mall to the Trooping the Colour ceremony.

main.desc: British man who shot blanks at Elizabeth II

events.text: At the Trooping the Colour ceremony in London, a teenager, Marcus Sarjeant, fires six blank shots at Queen Elizabeth II.

main.desc: Military ceremony in the British Army and other Commonwealth militaries

events.text: Fahd becomes King of Saudi Arabia upon the death of his brother, Khalid.

main.desc: King of Saudi Arabia from 1982 to 2005

events.text: Battles of Tumbledown and Wireless Ridge, during the Falklands War.
Pioneer 10 passed the orbit of Neptune, becoming the first man-made object to leave the proximity of the major planets of the Solar System.

main.desc: First spacecraft to visit Jupiter and the outer Solar System (1972–2003)

events.text: Pioneer 10 becomes the first man-made object to leave the central Solar System when it passes beyond the orbit of Neptune.

main.desc: First spacecraft to visit Jupiter and the outer Solar System (1972–2003)

events.text: First day of the June 1990 Mineriad in Romania. At least 240 strikers and students are arrested or killed in the chaos ensuing from the first post-Ceaușescu elections.

main.desc: Riot of protesters and miners in Bucharest

events.text: A jury in Anchorage, Alaska, blames recklessness by Exxon and Captain Joseph Hazelwood for the Exxon Valdez disaster, allowing victims of the oil spill to seek $15 billion in damages.
The Montana Freemen surrender after an 81-day standoff with FBI agents.
Garuda Indonesia flight 865 crashes during takeoff from Fukuoka Airport, killing three people and injuring 170.
A jury sentences Timothy McVeigh to death for his part in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.
The Uphaar Cinema Fire takes place at Green Park, Delhi, resulting in the deaths of 59 people and seriously injuring 103 others.
BMW win 1999 24 Hours of Le Mans.
President Kim Dae-jung of South Korea meets Kim Jong-il, leader of North Korea, for the beginning of the first ever inter-Korea summit, in the northern capital of Pyongyang.

main.desc: President of South Korea from 1998 to 2003

events.text: Italy pardons Mehmet Ali Ağca, the Turkish gunman who tried to kill Pope John Paul II in 1981.
The United States withdraws from the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty.

main.desc: 1972 arms control treaty between the United States and the Soviet Union

events.text: The jury acquits pop singer Michael Jackson of all charges for allegedly sexually abusing a child in 2003.

main.desc: 2005 child abuse trial of American singer

events.text: Insurgents carried out a second bombing at the al-Askari Mosque, one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam.

main.desc: Formally unclaimed attack on a Shia Islamic mosque in the Iraqi city of Samarra

events.text: The Al Askari Mosque is bombed for a second time.

main.desc: 10th-century Shia mosque and mausoleum in Iraq

events.text: A capsule of the Japanese spacecraft Hayabusa, containing particles of the asteroid 25143 Itokawa, returns to Earth by landing in the Australian Outback.

main.desc: Japanese probe to asteroid and sample return (2003–2010)

events.text: A 6.0 Mw earthquake (aftermath pictured) caused up to NZ$6 billion of additional damage to Christchurch, New Zealand, which was still recovering from an earthquake four months earlier.
A series of bombings across Iraq, including Baghdad, Hillah and Kirkuk, kills at least 93 people and wounds over 300 others.

main.desc: Bombings and shootings in Iraq during the post-U.S. insurgency

events.text: Some of the closest advisors and collaborators of Czech prime minister Petr Nečas were arrested for corruption.
Volkswagen is fined one billion euros over the emissions scandal.
A gas explosion in Zhangwan district of Shiyan city, in Hubei province of China, kills at least 12 people and wounds over 138 others.
At least 100 people are killed when a wedding boat capsizes on the Niger River in Kwara State, Nigeria.
Three people are killed and another three injured in an early morning stabbing and van ramming attack in Nottingham, England.

main.desc: Vehicle-ramming and stabbing attacks in England

events.text: Israel initiates air strikes against Iran, initiating the Twelve Day War.
The city of Munich is founded by Henry the Lion on the banks of the river Isar.
First Barons' War: Prince Louis of France takes the city of Winchester, abandoned by John, King of England, and soon conquers over half of the kingdom.

main.desc: Civil war in the Kingdom of England

events.text: While in exile in Fuzhou, away from the advancing Mongol invaders, the remnants of the Song dynasty court hold the coronation ceremony for Emperor Duanzong.

links.t: Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty

events.text: Second Mongol invasion of Vietnam: Forces led by Prince Trần Quang Khải of the Trần dynasty destroy most of the invading Mongol naval fleet in a battle at Chuong Duong.
Kublai Khan defeats the force of Nayan and other traditionalist Borjigin princes in East Mongolia and Manchuria.

main.desc: Emperor of Yuan China from 1271 to 1294

events.text: During the Peasants' Revolt in England, rebels stormed the Tower of London, killing Simon Sudbury, Lord Chancellor, and Robert Hales, Lord High Treasurer (both pictured).
Richard II of England meets leaders of the Peasants' Revolt at Mile End. The Tower of London is stormed by rebels who enter without resistance.
Welsh rebel leader Owain Glyndŵr, having declared himself Prince of Wales, allies himself with the French against King Henry IV of England.
Joris Veseler prints the first Dutch newspaper Courante uyt Italien, Duytslandt, &c. in Amsterdam (approximate date).

main.desc: First Dutch newspaper, published in June 1618

events.text: First English Civil War: Prince Maurice abandoned his siege of Lyme Regis in Dorset after learning of the approach of a Parliamentarian relief force.

main.desc: Part of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms (1642–1646)

events.text: English Civil War: Battle of Naseby: Twelve thousand Royalist forces are beaten by fifteen thousand Parliamentarian soldiers.
Franco-Spanish War: French and Spanish fleets fought the inconclusive Battle of Orbetello, with sailing vessels of both sides having to be towed into action by galleys due to light winds.

main.desc: Part of the Thirty Years' War

events.text: Franco-Spanish War: Turenne and the French army win a decisive victory over the Spanish at the battle of the Dunes.

main.desc: Part of the Thirty Years' War

links.t: Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Viscount of Turenne

events.text: A four day long naval engagement between the Dutch and English fleet ends, with the English suffering heavier losses.

main.desc: Large naval battle in June 1666 between England and the Netherlands; Dutch victory

events.text: King William III of England (William of Orange) lands in Ireland to confront the former King James II.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1689 to 1702

events.text: War of Jenkins' Ear: Spanish troops stormed the British-held strategically crucial position of Fort Mose in Spanish Florida.
American Revolutionary War: the Continental Army is established by the Continental Congress, marking the birth of the United States Armed Forces.
The Second Continental Congress adopted the stars and stripes design for the flag of the United States.
The Second Continental Congress passes the Flag Act of 1777 adopting the Stars and Stripes as the Flag of the United States.
Mutiny on the Bounty: HMS Bounty mutiny survivors including Captain William Bligh and 18 others reach Timor after a nearly 7,400 km (4,600 mi) journey in an open boat.

main.desc: 1789 mutiny aboard the British Royal Navy ship HMS Bounty

events.text: War of the Second Coalition: In the Battle of Marengo, Napoleonic forces secured victory over the Habsburgs when defeat had appeared inevitable until the arrival of French troops led by Louis Desaix.

main.desc: Second war on revolutionary France by European monarchies

events.text: The French Army of First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte defeats the Austrians at the Battle of Marengo in Northern Italy and re-conquers Italy.
Emperor Napoleon's French Grande Armée defeats the Russian Army at the Battle of Friedland in Poland (modern Russian  Kaliningrad Oblast) ending the War of the Fourth Coalition.
Badi VII, king of Sennar, surrenders his throne and realm to Ismail Pasha, general of the Ottoman Empire, bringing the 300 year old Sudanese kingdom to an end.

main.desc: Final ruler of the Funj Sultanate from 1805 to 1821

events.text: In a paper presented to the Royal Astronomical Society, English mathematician Charles Babbage proposed a difference engine (pictured), an automatic, mechanical calculator designed to tabulate polynomial functions.
Charles Babbage proposes a difference engine in a paper to the Royal Astronomical Society.
Beginning of the French colonization of Algeria: Thirty-four thousand French soldiers begin their invasion of Algiers, landing 27 kilometers west at Sidi Fredj.

main.desc: French colony and later intergral part in Northern Africa from 1830 to 1962

events.text: Henley Royal Regatta: the village of Henley-on-Thames, on the River Thames in Oxfordshire, stages its first regatta.
